title: A Layout-Aware Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Mitigating Hallucination in Turkish Texts: Evidence from the Turkish Official Gazette
content: Large language models (LLMs) hallucinate, limiting their trustworthy use in zero-error-tolerance domains such as law. We present a layout-aware, hybrid retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system for answering questions over the Turkish Official Gazette, the most binding source in the Turkish legal system. The pipeline uses IBM Docling for hierarchical layout analysis, preserving the article-paragraph-subparagraph hierarchy and table integrity of 30 Official Gazette issues (July 2025), and indexes content in PostgreSQL/pgvector with a local multilingual embedding model combined with a lexical index, keeping retrieval under local data sovereignty; response synthesis is delegated to claude-sonnet-5 under a citation-constrained prompt. On 33 original legal queries, the system answered 17/33 with a 4.2% hallucination rate (groundedness = 0.958), 81.8% citation accuracy, and Hit-Rate@8 = 0.786, versus only 1/33 for a zero-shot baseline. A component ablation (n = 25) showed layout-aware parsing and hybrid retrieval jointly raising Hit-Rate@8 from 61.6% to 100.0% while cutting hallucination from 15.4% to 0.0%. An independent legal-expert review rated 30/33 responses fully correct and all 33 validly cited. These results show that combining local, layout-aware retrieval with cloud-based generation can bring hallucination in Turkish question answering below the 17-33% band reported for leading commercial legal-AI tools.
